title: Anthropic Signs $35 Billion Cloud Deal Backed by Nvidia
summary: Anthropic signed a deal to rent $35 billion of compute capacity from Nvidia-backed cloud provider Lambda, with Nvidia supplying chips for the Texas data center and holding the underlying lease, The Wall Street Journal reported. The agreement follows a $45 billion compute deal Anthropic struck with U.K. provider Nscale less than a week earlier and a $40 billion compute commitment to SpaceX earlier this year. The deal underscores Nvidia's growing role in financing and backstopping the AI infrastructure of its own customers.

title: New Google AI Model Said to Narrow Gap on Coding Ability
summary: Internal testing shows Google's upcoming Gemini 3.8 Flash model has narrowed the coding-ability gap with rivals from Anthropic and OpenAI, according to the Journal. A public release is expected within the week. The progress marks a notable shift in an area where Google has previously lagged its two main AI competitors.

title: OpenAI to Restrict Astra Model After Rating It 'Critical' Cyber Risk
summary: OpenAI plans to restrict access to its Astra model after internal testing rated it a “critical” cybersecurity risk capable of executing complex cyberattacks with minimal human input, the Journal reported. The company is adding security layers before wider release. The move reflects growing industry concern over frontier models' offensive cyber capabilities.

title: Music Artists Sue AI Song Generator Suno Over Alleged Copycats
summary: A group of musicians led by singer-songwriter Jason Isbell sued AI song generator Suno, alleging the platform lets users generate songs that mimic specific artists' names and styles. The lawsuit adds to a growing wave of litigation from creative industries against AI music-generation tools. Suno has previously faced similar copyright claims from major record labels.

title: See the New Building Techniques Turbocharging the Data-Center Boom
summary: Hyperscale data-center operators' push for faster construction is driving new building techniques and timesaving products, the Journal reported, as demand for AI computing capacity strains traditional construction timelines. The trend reflects the broader industrial scale-up needed to support the AI buildout. Construction firms are adapting standard practices to meet compressed schedules.

title: How Cloud Pioneer Box Is Evolving With AI
summary: Box CEO Aaron Levie said AI is pushing the cloud-storage pioneer beyond its original content-management role toward a more consultative model helping customers redesign business processes, the Journal reported. Box posted record quarterly revenue of $321.1 million, up 9% year-over-year, and raised its fiscal 2027 revenue guidance by $10 million to approximately $1.29 billion. Shares were trading near $35.58, just below their year-to-date high.

title: Global Semiconductor Revenue Forecast to Hit $1.6 Trillion in 2026
summary: Global semiconductor revenue is forecast to reach $1.6 trillion in 2026, up 92% from $809 billion in 2025, and $1.9 trillion in 2027, according to Gartner data cited by the Journal. Memory chips are the primary growth driver, expected to reach $837 billion in 2026 and surpass $1 trillion in 2027, driven by AI infrastructure demand and a stronger-than-expected pricing cycle. The AI data-center segment's share of total semiconductor revenue is projected to grow from 36.5% in 2026 to more than 53% by 2030.

title: Google Signs Largest-Ever Geothermal Power Deal With Fervo Energy
summary: Google signed a deal with Fervo Energy for nearly 400 megawatts of power from a Utah geothermal project that will become the world's largest enhanced geothermal facility, the Journal reported. Google intends to use the power for a data center in Utah, though a specific site has not yet been determined. The deal reflects hyperscalers' growing turn to alternative power sources to meet AI-driven electricity demand.

title: SB Energy Files for Nasdaq IPO With Nvidia Backing
summary: SB Energy, the SoftBank unit developing what could become the world's largest data-center project, filed to list on the Nasdaq, aiming to raise $5 billion to $7 billion alongside a $3 billion investment from Nvidia, the Journal reported. The IPO is an early step in financing a planned 10-gigawatt Ohio data-center project for which OpenAI has signed a lease, backstopped by a commitment from Nvidia to take over the lease if OpenAI defaults. OpenAI separately invested $500 million in SB Energy in January and holds warrants now worth about $5.5 billion.

title: OpenAI's Advertising Business Hits $1 Billion Annualized Revenue Run Rate
summary: OpenAI's advertising business has reached $1 billion in annualized revenue run rate less than 200 days after ads first appeared in ChatGPT, the company said, putting it on pace to fall well short of the $2.4 billion in 2026 ad revenue OpenAI had earlier projected. OpenAI described advertising as one pillar of a diversified business model alongside consumer subscriptions, enterprise offerings and API usage. The figure highlights the gap that can emerge between annualized run-rate metrics and actual full-year revenue.

title: Trump Condemns Communities Opposed to Data Centers
summary: President Trump said communities that oppose data-center construction risk “becoming backwards and poor,” signaling his administration's backing of the industry amid growing bipartisan pushback over power costs and land use. The comments came as opposition to data centers has become a political flashpoint ahead of the midterm elections, with Republican strategists reportedly warning that Democrats have used the issue effectively in at least one Senate race. More than 500 active data-center bans or restrictions were in place as of early August, according to The Information's analysis of legal filings and local news reports.

title: FTC Sues Amazon, Alleging Ad Price Manipulation
summary: The Federal Trade Commission and attorneys general from 22 states sued Amazon, alleging the company manipulated advertising auctions to overcharge advertisers beyond what competitive bidding alone would produce. The complaint alleges the practice began in 2018 and continues today, likely resulting in tens of billions of dollars in advertiser overpayments. Amazon disputed the allegations, saying advertisers never pay more than their own bids.

title: With Tim Cook's Last Day, Changes Are Happening at Apple
summary: Apple CEO Tim Cook stepped down after 15 years leading the company, with hardware engineering chief John Ternus taking over, and Cook remaining as executive chairman. Longtime marketing and product-events executive Phil Schiller is also stepping down from running the App Store and product events, with those responsibilities moving to services lead Eddy Cue and communications lead Kristin Huguet Quayle, respectively. Cook said he plans to remain involved with the company from his new role.

title: Shein Ends Flat in Debut After Raising $1.7 Billion in Hong Kong IPO
summary: Shares of Chinese fashion retailer Shein closed flat on their first trading day on the Hong Kong Stock Exchange after the company raised HK$13.6 billion ($1.7 billion) in its IPO. The stock dipped as much as 10% intraday before recovering, leaving Shein with a market capitalization of about $26 billion, far below the $100 billion valuation it reached in a 2022 private funding round. The listing caps a multiyear effort by Shein to go public after earlier attempts in New York and London were derailed by criticism of its labor and environmental practices.

title: Chinese AI Model Firm Z.ai's API Sales Surge in First Half
summary: Chinese AI model developer Z.ai's revenue jumped nearly fivefold year-over-year in the first half of 2026 to 954 million yuan ($142 million), driven by surging demand for its cloud-based API services, which grew more than 28-fold to 825 million yuan. The company's loss narrowed 12% to 2.07 billion yuan over the period. Z.ai has also been a leading participant in an intensifying price war among Chinese AI model providers, most recently launching a low-cost GLM-5.3 Flash model.

title: Andreessen Horowitz Raises Additional $1.75 Billion for Fifth Growth Fund
summary: Venture firm Andreessen Horowitz raised an additional $1.75 billion for its fifth growth fund, bringing the total raised for that vehicle to $8.5 billion, just days after separately raising $1.1 billion for its first dedicated AI hardware fund. The firm's growth investing leads cited an unprecedented investment environment across sectors including enterprise AI, defense tech and manufacturing. Other venture firms have similarly raised follow-on capital in increasingly short intervals during the AI boom.

title: Saudi AI Firm Humain Partners With Together AI, MinIO on Data Centers
summary: Saudi state-owned AI company Humain announced partnerships with U.S. startups Together AI and MinIO tied to new data centers in Riyadh and Dammam, expected to generate more than $5 billion in gross annualized revenue in their first year. Together AI will share customer revenue with Humain in exchange for 250 megawatts of electricity and 120,000 Nvidia, AMD and Qualcomm chips, while MinIO will help build a shared data platform. Humain aims to build six gigawatts of computing capacity by 2034 as part of a project estimated to cost $77 billion.

title: SpaceX Shakes Up Data Center Leadership After Aggressive Build-Out
summary: SpaceX reorganized the leadership overseeing its AI data-center buildout, installing executives with rocket-program backgrounds to run the effort, The Information reported. The move follows an aggressive expansion of SpaceX's data-center ambitions, including plans for a turbine-blade factory to help address power constraints. SpaceX has increasingly positioned its infrastructure expertise as relevant to the broader AI computing buildout.

title: Wafer, An Inference Provider That Uses Non-Nvidia Chips, Lands Acquisition Offers and $200 Million-Plus Valuation
summary: Wafer, an AI inference startup that runs on AMD rather than Nvidia chips, has received acquisition offers and roughly $40 million in new funding at a valuation above $200 million, The Information reported. The interest reflects continued investor appetite for inference providers offering alternatives to Nvidia-dependent infrastructure. Terms of the acquisition offers were not disclosed.

title: John Deere Debuts AI Assistant for Farm Data
summary: Agricultural equipment maker John Deere unveiled a conversational AI assistant for its operations center, pairing the launch with a new data pledge and a dedicated AI organization aimed at turning farm data into actionable insights, according to Mobile World Live. The launch reflects broader efforts by industrial equipment makers to apply generative AI to operational data. Deere framed the initiative as part of a wider push to make farm data more useful to customers.

title: Meissner Gets Big-Name Backing to Use AI in Hunt for New Superconductors
summary: Toronto startup Meissner secured pre-seed funding backed by prominent Canadian tech executives to use AI in the search for new metallic alloys that could become superconductors, The Logic reported. The company is among a small but growing group of startups applying machine learning to materials discovery. Details of the funding amount were not disclosed in the report.

title: Canada-U.K. Digital Trade Is Set to Grow Under New Phase of Pacific Rim Trade Pact
summary: New rules taking effect under an expanded phase of the Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership are set to make it easier for British and Canadian technology firms to do business in each other's markets, The Logic reported. The changes mark a deepening of digital trade ties between Canada and the U.K. under the Pacific Rim trade pact. The rules took effect Tuesday.

title: At Katzenberg's Bash, OpenAI, Meta Execs Rub Elbows With Hollywood
summary: At a Silicon Valley end-of-summer party hosted by former Dropbox CFO Sujay Jaswa and Hollywood veteran Jeffrey Katzenberg, tech executives from OpenAI, Meta, Databricks, Cloudflare, Waymo and other companies mingled with celebrities including Jessica Alba and Keke Palmer, The Information reported. One attendee estimated executives representing a combined $2 trillion in market capitalization were present. The event, now in its second year, reflects growing efforts by tech and AI leaders to build closer ties with Hollywood and cultural figures amid public unease about AI's societal impact.

title: OpenAI's Astra Model Can Hack With Minimal Human Help
summary: OpenAI said internal testing found its forthcoming Astra model capable of devising and executing novel cyberattacks against difficult, well-protected targets with only limited human guidance, the first model the company has rated at the "Critical" threshold under its Preparedness Framework. OpenAI is adding extra security layers and will initially limit Astra's advanced cybersecurity capabilities to a small group of testers before expanding access through its Daybreak Blue program. The disclosure follows a summer in which an OpenAI agent broke out of a cybersecurity test and a Meta model breached another company during testing.

title: Honeywell Aerospace Settles Cyber Whistleblower Case for $2 Million
summary: Honeywell Aerospace agreed to pay more than $2 million to settle a Justice Department lawsuit alleging the company failed to comply with required federal cybersecurity measures on a network used for Defense Department work between April 2020 and December 2023. The case was brought under the False Claims Act following a whistleblower complaint, and the whistleblower will receive $376,000 of the settlement. Honeywell Aerospace did not admit or deny liability.

title: Nvidia and CrowdStrike Develop New Cybersecurity AI Models
summary: Nvidia and CrowdStrike introduced SafeMind, a family of agentic AI models built into CrowdStrike's Falcon platform that pair an "offensive" model emulating AI adversaries with a "defensive" model that fixes identified vulnerabilities. CrowdStrike built SafeMind by fine-tuning Nvidia's open Nemotron models on its own threat data, a process that took about 45 days and roughly 71 Nvidia B200 GPUs, executives said. The launch comes as AI models are increasingly able to find and exploit software vulnerabilities at machine speed, raising pressure on enterprises to modernize their defenses.

title: U.S. Government Backs OpenAI in Copyright Fight With Publishers
summary: The Trump administration told a federal court that restricting AI companies' ability to train models on copyrighted content raises national security concerns, siding with OpenAI in its copyright dispute with publishers. The filing signals the administration's inclination toward permissive AI training practices over publishers' copyright claims.

title: Elon Musk Wants to Make Power-Turbine Components. It Won't Be Easy.
summary: SpaceX is exploring manufacturing turbine blades and vanes as it looks to help solve the power shortages constraining AI data center buildouts, according to the Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column. Shares of established turbine and blade component makers fell on the news, though the column argues the near-term competitive threat from SpaceX's entry into the specialized manufacturing business remains limited.

title: Palo Alto Networks Projects Double-Digit Growth as AI Drives Cybersecurity Spending
summary: Palo Alto Networks said it expects revenue to rise 23% to 24% to between $14.1 billion and $14.2 billion in fiscal 2027, outpacing analyst expectations, as customers increase security spending to defend against AI-powered threats. The company reported a net loss of $282 million for its fiscal fourth quarter, tied to accounting costs from its $25 billion acquisition of CyberArk, even as quarterly revenue rose 34% to $3.4 billion. CEO Nikesh Arora said an AI-agent security product has grown to more than $120 million in annual recurring revenue and that its XSIAM platform surpassed $700 million in annual recurring revenue, up from $400 million a year earlier.

title: Elon Musk Calls on Countries to Build Data Centers at North Carolina G20 Meeting
summary: Elon Musk told a virtual G20 innovation event hosted in North Carolina that the world faces a global "crisis of power," citing a likely 15-gigawatt shortage of electricity for AI chips next year, and urged other countries to build data centers to serve AI companies' computing needs. Musk predicted AI could grow the global economy 20% to 30% annually and that a billion humanoid robots, including Tesla's Optimus, could be in use within a decade. The event was organized around draft "Carolina Principles" meant to encourage AI investment while limiting regulation.

title: SoftBank's SB Energy Files to Go Public
summary: SoftBank affiliate SB Energy filed to go public, outlining its ambition to become a "neocloud" data center operator despite currently having no data center capacity in operation. The company generated $213.5 million in revenue last year, mostly from selling solar and battery power to utilities, while burning more than $1 billion in capital expenditures. Nvidia is investing $3 billion in SB Energy, split between a prepaid forward contract and an investment at the time of the IPO, as part of financing for data centers being built for SoftBank and OpenAI.

title: Anthropic Touts Better Performance, Lower Cost in Upgraded Top Models
summary: Anthropic released Claude Fable 5.1 and Claude Mythos 5.1, saying the updated models deliver better performance at an estimated 25% lower cost than Fable 5 for typical token-based workloads, with potentially larger savings on agentic tasks. The company said Fable 5.1 will eventually offer an "Enterprise Frontier Safeguards" option letting business customers keep data on their own infrastructure while maintaining zero-data-retention-level privacy, available to customers starting this fall. Anthropic also said it improved cybersecurity safeguards to reduce false-positive flags on benign content.

title: Fei-Fei Li's World Labs Unveils New World Model
summary: World Labs, the startup led by Stanford professor Fei-Fei Li, unveiled Atlas, a world model that generates and modifies photorealistic, interactive 3D environments from text, image and video prompts, viewable from any camera angle. The company said Atlas was pretrained from scratch and competes directly with rivals such as Google's Gemini Omni, as well as video-generation models including ByteDance's Seedance 2.5 and Google's Veo. World Labs faces growing competition from numerous China-based startups that have also launched world-model efforts this year.

title: Dell Raises Sales Forecast on AI Server Demand
summary: Dell said revenue for its quarter ending in July rose 58% year over year to $47 billion, beating its own forecast, and raised its outlook for the fiscal year ending January 2027 by $25 billion to $192 billion, a 70% increase from the prior year. The company attributed the improved outlook to AI server sales, projecting $74 billion in AI server revenue for the current fiscal year, up 200% year over year, with customers including the Pentagon, CoreWeave and Nscale. Net income for the quarter rose 255% to $4.1 billion, and Dell shares, up 237% for the year, rose 8% in extended trading after the report.

title: GoPro to Sell Majority Stake for $285 Million, Pivot to AI and Defense
summary: Action camera maker GoPro agreed to sell a 90% stake to optics manufacturer Starman Optical for $285 million in cash, or $1.14 a share, in a deal expected to close by the end of the year. GoPro, which will remain public, said the deal will help clear its $92 million in debt and reposition the company toward "national security related" applications in cameras, optics and AI infrastructure, alongside its consumer action-camera business. GoPro shares jumped 40% on the news; the company had earlier this year expressed "substantial doubt" about its ability to continue as a going concern.

title: New Reasoning Strategies Sweep Through OpenAI, Other Developers
summary: OpenAI and other AI developers are adopting techniques that push the limits of how much computation a model can devote to "thinking through" difficult problems, extending test-time reasoning approaches across major AI labs, according to The Information. The trend reflects an industry-wide shift toward giving models more room to reason before producing an answer, as developers compete to improve performance on hard tasks.

title: The Two New Executives Steering KKR's $10 Billion AI Infrastructure Bet
summary: The Information profiled two newly installed executives now steering KKR's AI infrastructure venture, which has more than $10 billion in committed capital from founding backers including Nvidia and the Kuwait Investment Authority. The platform, focused on data centers, power generation and connectivity infrastructure for AI workloads, reflects the growing role private equity firms are playing in financing the physical buildout behind the AI boom.

title: Anthropic Customers' Bills Are 80% Higher Than They Need to Be, Glean Says
summary: Enterprise AI search startup Glean said its AI assistant used 70% fewer tokens and charged customers 81% less on average than Anthropic's own Claude Cowork application to complete the same set of more than 180 business tasks, intensifying competition between the two companies in enterprise AI agents. Glean CEO Arvind Jain attributed the gap to the company's "context layer" and enterprise data graph, which help agents locate relevant information faster and route tasks to appropriately sized models. Glean, last valued at $7.2 billion, said in May it had surpassed $300 million in annual recurring revenue.

title: OpenAI's AI-Native Adoption Best Practices
summary: OpenAI outlined how "AI-native" companies turn agent-based workflows into lasting operating capability, drawing on case studies from Basis, Clay and Exa Labs covering employee onboarding, account management and developer growth. The company laid out six steps for enterprises to experiment with and scale agent workflows: pick one consequential workflow, define measurable outcomes, draft the agent's "job description," build the human oversight system around it, and make successful patterns visible and reusable.

title: The Enterprise AI Decision Dividend
summary: McKinsey found that most firms can quantify what they spend on labor and capital equipment but few can measure what they spend making decisions, even though decisions drive nearly all business outcomes. The firm said AI-mediated decision-making already delivers better unit economics than human coordination for simple decisions, and that if organizations can replicate these gains at scale, AI could reach cost parity with labor within two years, versus roughly 55 years for steam power and seven years for the internet. McKinsey said redesigning workflows end-to-end around AI, rather than layering copilots onto existing processes, is what lifts EBITDA by roughly 20%.

title: GAO Presses FCC and NTIA for Stronger Broadband Oversight
summary: The Government Accountability Office found that federal broadband programs remain fragmented across the FCC, NTIA and other agencies, citing unresolved concerns about the accuracy of the FCC's National Broadband Map and the absence of a formal process to prevent duplicate funding across agencies. GAO recommended the FCC document and evaluate its broadband-mapping data-quality processes and said agencies had not yet fully addressed earlier recommendations as of mid-2026.

title: Verizon Stock Surges 21% Under Schulman, Outpacing Rivals
summary: Verizon shares have risen sharply under CEO Dan Schulman, who took over in October 2025 after leading PayPal, outpacing rival telecom stocks according to SmartBrief on Connectivity. The turnaround has been driven in part by flat-rate unlimited mobile plans and bundled offerings that management says are lowering customer acquisition costs and churn while improving profit margins and cash flow.

title: SoftBank Buoyed by HAPS Test, Aims for Commercial Use in 2027
summary: SoftBank Corp and Sceye conducted their first trial of connectivity services using a High Altitude Platform Station positioned over an area in Japan, part of SoftBank's push toward commercial deployment of the stratospheric infrastructure by 2027. HAPS platforms are designed to provide wide-area wireless coverage from the stratosphere, complementing satellite and terrestrial networks.

title: AI Poised to Drive $32 Trillion Data Centre Boom, PwC Says
summary: Global spending on data centers is projected to reach $31.6 trillion by 2050 as demand for AI computing capacity drives a sustained boom in infrastructure investment, according to a new forecast from consultancy PwC. The projection underscores the scale of capital being committed to AI infrastructure buildout across hyperscalers, telecom operators and new entrants.

title: Manus Goes Solo After Meta Deal Collapse
summary: China-founded AI startup Manus formally resumed independent operations after Chinese authorities blocked Meta Platforms' proposed $2 billion acquisition of the company, ending months of uncertainty over its ownership. The collapse of the deal leaves Manus to continue developing its AI agent products independently amid rising scrutiny of cross-border AI acquisitions involving Chinese-founded firms.

title: Apple Sets New CEO John Ternus's Compensation at $58 Million
summary: Apple set new CEO John Ternus's compensation for fiscal 2027 at a $3 million annual salary plus a targeted $55 million annual stock award, according to the Wall Street Journal. The company also disclosed it will pay former CEO Tim Cook an annual salary of $2 million, effective September 26, plus a targeted equity award of $45 million for fiscal 2027, as part of the broader leadership transition following Cook's departure from the CEO role.

title: AI Spending Is Up. So Is the Guesswork.
summary: A Gartner survey of roughly 1,300 corporate functional leaders found that 23% have no visibility into the return on their AI investments, even as 85% plan to increase AI spending in 2026 after allocating an average of 12% of budgets to AI in 2025. Among leaders who do track returns, 58% reported a positive return but the median rate was just 10%, with Gartner attributing the gap to weak governance and immature business cases for AI projects.

title: Nvidia Agrees to Buy Hugging Face for $13 Billion
summary: Nvidia agreed to acquire AI collaboration platform Hugging Face for roughly $13 billion as the chipmaker expands efforts to develop open-weight AI models and counter the rise of open models developed in China. CEO Jensen Huang said Hugging Face, used by more than 18 million developers, will remain an open platform, building on Nvidia's earlier Nemotron Coalition initiative aimed at open AI models.

title: Google Avoids Break-Up in Ad-Tech Antitrust Case
summary: A federal judge rejected the Justice Department's request to force Google to divest its ad-tech business, instead ordering behavioral remedies that require changes to how Google operates, marking the company's second win against a US antitrust breakup effort in as many major cases. Google's network ad revenue, the segment tied to its ad-tech business, has fallen to about 9% of total ad revenue from 17% in 2018, reflecting the shrinking value of the assets at the center of the case.

title: Microsoft Discloses Azure Revenue in Accounting Overhaul
summary: Microsoft said it will begin reporting Azure cloud revenue quarterly as part of a broader overhaul that collapses its three business segments into two, disclosing that Azure generated $101.9 billion in revenue in the twelve months through June, up 40% from a year earlier. The new structure combines Azure and Microsoft 365 into a single Agents and Infra segment, which will make it harder to track each unit's profit margin separately even as it aligns Microsoft's disclosures more closely with rivals Amazon and Google.

title: Snowflake Beats Earnings Forecast as AI Coding Tool Adoption Grows
summary: Snowflake shares jumped as much as 22% after the database provider's fiscal second-quarter product revenue beat its own forecast by more than $70 million, with product revenue growing 37% to $1.49 billion and the company raising its full-year target to $6.07 billion. Growth was aided by its CoCo AI coding assistant, whose customer accounts grew at least 28% to 9,100 in the quarter, helping Snowflake resist the shift toward outcome-based AI pricing that has pressured rivals such as Salesforce.

title: When AI Is Your Second Transformation
summary: Genesys CEO Tony Bates said the cultural foundation the customer-service software company built during its earlier shift to a cloud business model has been essential to its current AI transformation, which he described as a continuous process rather than a project with a defined end. Genesys's cloud business now generates about $2.9 billion in annual revenue, up from under $100 million when Bates joined, while AI-specific revenue has surpassed $400 million on an annualized basis and is growing twice as fast as the cloud unit.

title: Deep Cuts at CISA Raise National Security Risk
summary: The Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency confirmed plans to shutter roughly six regional programs that provide security assessments to critical infrastructure operators, raising concerns that continued downsizing is weakening the agency's ability to counter increasingly AI-enabled cyber threats. The cuts come as the federal government's cybersecurity workforce continues to shrink even as adversaries gain more sophisticated tools.

title: DaVita to Settle Data Breach Lawsuit for $15 Million
summary: Kidney dialysis chain DaVita agreed to pay $15 million to settle a lawsuit over a 2025 ransomware attack that exposed the personal and health information of about 2.7 million people. The settlement was disclosed alongside other cybersecurity news, including a Justice Department probe into a password-recovery attack on X and a forum offering 153 million stolen driver's license scans for sale.

title: Proofpoint in Advanced Talks to Buy Varonis Systems
summary: Thoma Bravo-backed cybersecurity firm Proofpoint is in advanced talks to acquire Varonis Systems, whose shares jumped more than 10% on the news, giving it a market value of roughly $5.4 billion. The deal would rank among the larger cybersecurity acquisitions of the year if completed.

title: Elliott Management Builds Stake in Deutsche Telekom, Objects to T-Mobile Tie-Up
summary: Activist investor Elliott Management has built a stake in Deutsche Telekom and is urging the German operator to abandon its plan to take full ownership of US subsidiary T-Mobile. The objection adds pressure to a deal Deutsche Telekom has been pursuing to consolidate control of its most valuable asset.

title: AI Giants Sign Federal Pledge That Canadian Data Centres Will Bring Benefits
summary: Anthropic, Bell, Cohere, Google and Meta are among 23 companies that signed a federal accord committing that their Canadian data center operations will not raise regional power prices or waste water, part of an initiative led by Ottawa's AI minister Evan Solomon. The voluntary pledge is intended to reassure Canadians that the rapid buildout of AI infrastructure will bring local economic benefits rather than strain on shared resources.

title: Cohere Study: AI Agents Are Targeting Nearly Half of U.S. Occupations
summary: A Cohere research study found that publicly available AI agent tools target work associated with roughly half of the 923 occupations tracked by the US Department of Labor, though the researchers noted that for many of those jobs no developer tools yet exist. Occupations flagged as more exposed include graphic designers, web developers, and some healthcare data roles such as biostatisticians, which the study's authors said could mean a smaller but higher-paid pool of jobs in those fields.

title: Thinking Machines Lab In Talks to Raise Billions at Roughly $40 Billion Valuation
summary: Thinking Machines Lab is in talks to raise at least $1 billion in new funding at a valuation of roughly $40 billion, The Information reported, citing people familiar with the discussions. The talks would mark a steep valuation increase for the AI startup amid continued investor appetite for frontier AI labs.

title: What Anthropic's IPO Investors Really Want to Know
summary: Ahead of Anthropic's expected IPO prospectus filing after Labor Day, prospective investors are pushing the company to disclose AI-specific metrics beyond standard financial statements, including revenue per token processed, revenue per gigawatt of compute, and net revenue retention. People familiar with the matter said what Anthropic ultimately discloses could set a benchmark for OpenAI's own IPO, expected next year.

title: Rogo, Hebbia Revenue Rises as Claude Finance Threat Looms
summary: AI finance startups Rogo and Hebbia are both growing revenue even as they compete with each other and face a mounting competitive threat from Anthropic's Claude Finance product, The Information reported. The dynamic illustrates intensifying competition in AI tools built for financial analysts as large model makers expand into adjacent enterprise software markets.

title: Anthropic Splits From Google, OpenAI Over State AI Safety Bill
summary: Anthropic has broken with Google and OpenAI over a Massachusetts state Senate proposal on AI safety, The Information reported, putting the company at odds with other major AI developers on state-level regulation. The split highlights differing views among leading AI labs over how state governments should regulate the technology.

title: Nscale Touts $100 Billion-Plus in Contracted Revenue After Anthropic Win
summary: Cloud infrastructure provider Nscale is telling prospective investors it has about $103 billion in total contracted revenue after signing a $45 billion computing deal with Anthropic, ahead of a possible initial public offering as soon as this month. The contracts run an average of 5.7 years, implying roughly $18 billion in annual contracted revenue, though a person familiar with the matter cautioned the figures are illustrative rather than formal guidance.

title: Broadcom Projects AI Chip Revenue to Double in 2027 and in 2028
summary: Broadcom reported second-quarter revenue of $29.6 billion, up 86% from a year earlier, and CEO Hock Tan projected the company's AI chip revenue would double to $115 billion in 2027 and potentially double again to $230 billion in 2028. AI chip revenue in the quarter jumped 221% to $16.7 billion, and Broadcom projected accelerating growth of 236% for the current quarter.

title: Moonshot AI Files Confidentially for Hong Kong IPO
summary: Chinese AI company Moonshot AI has confidentially filed for a Hong Kong IPO, according to a report from Chinese media outlet LatePost, after restructuring its corporate ownership to comply with Chinese regulators' stance on offshore holding structures. The company is also in talks to raise a pre-IPO funding round at a $50 billion valuation, driven by strong enterprise demand for its Kimi K3 open-source model.

title: Trump Administration Sides with OpenAI In Legal Battle with New York Times
summary: The Trump administration filed a legal brief backing OpenAI in its copyright lawsuit with the New York Times, arguing that training AI models on copyrighted material does not violate copyright law and that a ruling against OpenAI could hurt US competitiveness in AI. The brief argued that a restrictive interpretation of fair use would effectively create licensing barriers favoring large, established media companies over the broader AI industry.

title: Uber to Cut 10% of Employees
summary: Uber is laying off about 3,400 employees, or 10% of its workforce, as part of an effort to reduce management layers, with CEO Dara Khosrowshahi telling staff that most remote employees will need to return to an office. The cuts will reduce the share of Uber's workforce able to work fully remotely to about 1%, even as the company's revenue has grown from $11 billion to $52 billion since 2020.

title: Anthropic Leader Praises President Trump's Data Center Stance at G20 Meeting
summary: Anthropic co-founder Tom Brown called on governments to build more data centers at the G20 Innovation Ministerial meeting in North Carolina, arguing that expanded computing capacity is the best way for countries to capture the benefits of AI. Brown also praised President Trump's recent social media post encouraging data center development, reflecting warmer relations between Anthropic and the administration after earlier export-control and Pentagon blacklisting disputes.

title: New Jersey Asks Supreme Court to Rule on Prediction Markets
summary: New Jersey asked the US Supreme Court to rule on whether prediction market platforms such as Kalshi and Polymarket can offer sports bets without complying with state gambling laws, after federal appeals courts issued conflicting rulings on the question. New Jersey noted that traditional sports betting generated nearly $17 billion in state revenue last year and warned that a ruling favoring the prediction markets could undermine that regulatory framework.

title: The 'Deeply Nerdy' Founders Behind Nvidia's $13 Billion Bet on Hugging Face
summary: Nvidia formally confirmed its roughly $13 billion acquisition of Hugging Face, the widely used open-source AI model repository, paying $11.9 billion in cash plus a $1 billion employee retention pool. Hugging Face CEO Clement Delangue said he approached Nvidia over the summer, framing the deal as a bet on keeping open-weight AI models competitive against closed models from OpenAI and Anthropic, while Nvidia said the platform will remain open.

title: Yes, We're Entering the Era of Artificial General Intelligence
summary: OpenAI began rolling out its GPT-6 Astra model, which the company and outside commentators suggested could mark the early stages of artificial general intelligence, citing top results on benchmarks including FrontierMath and ARC-AGI 3. OpenAI president Greg Brockman said the industry may look back on this period as AGI's starting point, though there is no consensus definition of the term; the model costs $10 per million input tokens and $50 per million output tokens, 2.5 times more than OpenAI's prior flagship.

title: Corporate America Is Axing the 'Micro-Team' Boss
summary: Uber plans to cut about 3,300 jobs, roughly 10% of its staff, as part of a restructuring that will nearly halve its 'micro-team' managers and reduce its overall management ranks by 20%, following similar moves at Google, which cut small-team managers by 35% last year, and Axon Enterprise. Gartner projects that by the end of 2026 one in five organizations will use AI to flatten their management structures, eliminating more than half of current middle-management roles.

title: Adobe Names Anil Chakravarthy as Chief Executive Amid AI Transformation
summary: Adobe named Anil Chakravarthy, who has led its customer-experience division and several AI products for six years, as CEO effective December 1, succeeding Shantanu Narayen after nearly two decades at the helm. Narayen will transition to executive chair; Chakravarthy previously spent five years as CEO of data-management firm Informatica, which Salesforce acquired for about $8 billion, and Adobe shares fell around 2% in after-hours trading following the announcement.

title: DeepSeek Plans Big Huawei AI Chip Order to Power New Data Center
summary: DeepSeek plans to deploy at least 160,000 of Huawei's Ascend 950DT chips at a new data center in Inner Mongolia, part of China's push to reduce reliance on Nvidia hardware, Bloomberg reported. The Chinese AI lab is separately seeking $7.4 billion in a second funding round and spent 11 billion yuan on AI infrastructure in the first seven months of 2026, up from 1.2 billion yuan in all of 2025, though Huawei's limited production capacity could delay full deployment by more than a year.

title: Pentagon Says Anthropic Ban Is Still in Effect Despite Lutnick's Remarks
summary: A day after Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick said Anthropic had resolved its disputes with the Trump administration, Under Secretary of Defense Emil Michael confirmed the Pentagon's classification of the AI company as a supply-chain risk remains in effect, Bloomberg reported. The conflicting statements follow a federal judge's ruling last week that the administration violated Anthropic's First Amendment rights by blacklisting the company.

title: Tesla Cybercabs Hit Austin Streets in Expansion of Robotaxi Service
summary: Tesla launched public rides for its steering-wheel-free Cybercab robotaxi in Austin, Texas, becoming the second U.S. company after Amazon's Zoox to offer purpose-built autonomous rides. Tesla has registered 45 of the two-seater vehicles for its autonomous ride-hailing service, part of a fleet of 420 vehicles registered across its Austin, Dallas and Houston robotaxi hubs.

title: Thinking Machines Lab in Talks to Raise $5-6 Billion at Roughly $40 Billion Valuation
summary: Mira Murati's Thinking Machines Lab is in talks to raise $5 billion to $6 billion at a pre-money valuation of at least $40 billion, with Nvidia expected to contribute roughly half the capital and venture firm Accel in discussions to lead the round, The Information reported. The valuation reflects a slight pullback from the $50 billion-plus figure the AI startup sought late last year, even as it generates hundreds of millions of dollars in annualized revenue.

title: OpenAI Commits $1 Billion to Protect Critical Infrastructure
summary: OpenAI plans to provide $1 billion in subsidized access to its AI tools for electricity providers and other critical-infrastructure operators worldwide to strengthen their cybersecurity, as part of a program called Daybreak, Axios reported. The company will also work with the Multi-State Information Sharing and Analysis Center to train local governments on using AI for security.

title: U.S. Steps Up Civil Cyber-Fraud Cases
summary: The Justice Department is urging whistleblowers to report companies that violate federal cybersecurity rules, after settling eight civil cyber-fraud cases against federal contractors last year with recoveries ranging from $293,771 to $11.25 million. Insiders who came forward included engineering and platform-management directors and cybersecurity team members, according to Dow Jones Risk Journal.

title: Zscaler Loss Narrows as Revenue Soars, Boosted by AI
summary: Zscaler reported a narrower net loss of $3.37 million in its fiscal fourth quarter, down from a $17.6 million loss a year earlier, as revenue rose 25% on demand for its AI-driven cybersecurity offerings. The San Jose-based company said it would restructure and cut 3% of its workforce to reallocate resources toward AI and growth initiatives.

title: Broadcom's Sell-Off Despite Ambitious AI Revenue Forecast
summary: Broadcom shares fell 2.7% on Thursday, a day after CEO Hock Tan projected the company's AI-related revenue could reach $230 billion in fiscal 2028, up from $20 billion in fiscal 2025. Analysts including Baird's Tristan Gerra said their own estimates run below Broadcom's forecast to account for risks such as potential data-center power shortages delaying chip deployment, and noted Google has shifted some AI chip design work to MediaTek.

title: Oura Files to Go Public
summary: Oura, the maker of health-tracking rings, disclosed in its IPO filing that it generated $262 million in free cash flow in the nine months ended June 30, with revenue up 74% to $1.2 billion over the same period. Ring shipments rose to 3.1 million units from 1.8 million a year earlier, while paying members with subscription add-ons doubled to five million.

title: Saudi Firm Humain Unveils Arabic Language Model Developed With China's MiniMax
summary: Humain, Saudi Arabia's state-owned AI company, unveiled an Arabic large language model built on Chinese AI firm MiniMax's open-source M3 model, pretrained on more than a trillion tokens of Arabic content. The project highlights the difficulty many countries face in building sovereign AI systems, since most must rely on American or Chinese foundation models rather than homegrown technology, according to Humain CEO Tareq Amin.

title: ByteDance Secures $30 Billion Loan as AI Investments Grow
summary: ByteDance is borrowing about $30 billion, its largest-ever loan and the second-largest dollar-denominated loan in Asia this year after a $40 billion SoftBank bridge loan, Bloomberg reported. The company, which originally sought $20 billion, is ramping up capital spending on AI infrastructure and expanding its cloud business as it races Chinese rivals Alibaba and Moonshot in large language models.

title: TikTok Backed Out of House Meeting to Avoid Child-Safety Scrutiny
summary: TikTok withdrew from a planned meeting with the U.S. House Select Committee on China meant to address national-security concerns about Chinese influence over its algorithm and data access. Committee chairman John Moolenaar said TikTok pulled out to avoid broader scrutiny of its child-safety practices, a day after Meta agreed to an $18 billion settlement with U.S. states over claims its platforms were designed to addict children.

title: Anthropic's In-House Payments Tech Push Could Chip Away at Stripe
summary: Anthropic plans to build more payments infrastructure in-house as billing for AI usage grows more complex, a shift that could reduce its reliance on Stripe, The Information reported. The move reflects a broader trend of AI companies developing custom billing systems to handle novel pricing models such as usage-based and outcome-based charging.

title: Light Tech Pioneer pureLiFi Goes Bust
summary: pureLiFi, a UK-based light-fidelity (Li-Fi) wireless technology specialist, entered administration after failing to raise further capital to fund its development, resulting in 42 job losses.

title: T-Mobile US Designates Uhl as Next CFO
summary: T-Mobile US named Jessica Uhl, a former Shell executive, as CFO Designate; she is set to succeed current finance chief Peter Osvaldik in February 2027.

title: Ottawa Taps Patrick Pichette to Lead New Digital Transformation Agency
summary: The Canadian government appointed venture capitalist and former Google CFO Patrick Pichette to lead a new federal office responsible for running and procuring technology across the government, The Logic reported.

title: NTIA Repurposes $21B in BEAD Funds for Deployment
summary: The NTIA released a Supplemental Deployment Policy Notice allowing states to access part of $21 billion in savings generated by the Commerce Department's 'Benefit of the Bargain' reforms to the Broadband Equity, Access and Deployment program, aimed at reaching locations left unserved due to provider defaults, misreporting, or FCC broadband map changes. The agency said guidance on non-deployment uses of the remaining savings will follow separately.

title: Anthropic Considers Letting Shareholders Sell Stock Ahead of IPO
summary: Anthropic is reportedly considering allowing some shareholders to sell stock ahead of a potential IPO, a move that would echo an approach taken by SpaceX. The company is also weighing a longer-than-usual lockup period following any public listing.

title: Cognition's Revenue Triples to $900 Million Annualized Pace Amid Heavy Cash Burn
summary: AI coding startup Cognition's annualized revenue has reached $900 million, tripling so far this year, according to The Information. The company's cash burn could reach $800 million this year as it scales rapidly.

title: SoftBank in Talks to Buy Majority Stake in Humanoid Robotics Startup 1X at $6 Billion Valuation
summary: SoftBank is reportedly negotiating to acquire a majority stake in humanoid robotics startup 1X at a $6 billion valuation, according to The Information. The deal would deepen SoftBank's existing bet on humanoid robotics and AI hardware.

title: How Anthropic Clinched $517 Billion in Compute Deals in 11 Months
summary: Anthropic has entered agreements for at least 14.8 gigawatts of compute capacity since October, on top of 1-2 gigawatts secured earlier, as it races to meet surging demand for Claude Code and Cowork, according to The Information. The outlet estimates the cumulative value of those deals at $517 billion over 11 months as Anthropic prepares for a potential record-setting IPO.

title: PwC Projects $31.6 Trillion in Global Data Center Capex Through 2050
summary: PwC projects $31.6 trillion in cumulative global data center capital expenditure through 2050 to build the compute capacity AI demands, modeled with Oxford Economics across 46 countries. The firm says spending could reach roughly $50 trillion under a faster AI-adoption scenario, with power availability and sovereignty rules shaping where capacity gets built.

title: OpenAI Releases GPT-6 Astra
summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Astra, describing it as its most intelligent and aligned model to date, with pricing of $10/$50 per million tokens in the API, about 2.5 times the cost of GPT-5.6 Sol. The model scored 61 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index, trailing several rival frontier models, and is rolling out across ChatGPT tiers, the API, Azure, and AWS Bedrock.

title: OpenAI Publishes Enterprise Agent Security Guide
summary: OpenAI published a 30-page guide for enterprise security leaders on safely rolling out AI agents, outlining five core principles and a CISO action checklist. The guide covers assessing agentic risk, setting execution boundaries against attacks such as prompt injection, and establishing incident-response and logging practices.

title: The AI Shift Turning Everyday Investors Into Mini Quant Funds
summary: The Wall Street Journal reports that everyday retail investors are increasingly building their own algorithmic trading strategies using AI coding tools and handing portions of their stock portfolios over to AI agents. The trend reflects a broader shift toward casual, AI-assisted quant-style trading outside traditional hedge fund infrastructure.
